recipes.name: Turkey Lettuce Wraps with Shiitake Mushrooms
ingredients_raw: 2 ounces mai fun (angel hair) rice noodles
4 teaspoons finely minced fresh ginger root

steps.text: Bring 2 cups water to a boil in a small saucepan; turn off heat. Stir in rice noodles, cover the saucepan, and soak until soft, 5 to 7 minutes. Rinse noodles with cold water. Drain well.
Heat 1 teaspoon vegetable oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add mushrooms; cook until brown and soft, about 2 minutes. Transfer mushrooms to a bowl; set aside.

Heat remaining 2 teaspoons vegetable oil in the same skillet. Add turkey; cook until no longer pink, 5 to 7 minutes. Stir in green onions, water chestnuts, ginger, and garlic; cook for 1 minute. Add reserved mushrooms, soy sauce, and sugar; simmer to combine flavors, 1 to 2 minutes. Off heat, stir in vinegar, sesame oil, and orange zest.
Divide turkey filling among lettuce leaves; top with cooked noodles, a sprinkle of carrots, bean sprouts, peanuts, and cilantro. Serve with sweet chili sauce for dipping.

raw_recipe.headline: Turkey Lettuce Wraps with Shiitake Mushrooms
raw_recipe.description: This turkey lettuce wraps with shiitake mushrooms recipe uses lean ground turkey, shiitake mushrooms, and lots of water chestnuts for a tasty filling.

review.reviewBody: very easy to make and delish I changed it a little no mushrooms or water chesnuts and added red and yellow peppers.

This is fabulously delicious, all the flavors make a great combination! I made a few slight adjustments, I seasoned the turkey with salt and pepper, I substituted baby portobello mushrooms, and I added 2 teaspoons Sambal(chili paste) because I like a little bit of heat. I did make my own Tamarind Cashew Dipping Sauce just as a preference. I always keep Mae Ploy Sweet Chili Sauce on hand, and my family loved the pairing of this sauce with the meal.

I made this with ground chicken. I followed the recipe fairly closely except for the omission of water chestnuts and some of the garnishes. It was a huge hit for me and my 12 year old. He said it was as good as restaurant food and actually ate a good amount of it (which is a struggle with him).

This recipe was great! Tasted so good, couldn't even tell it was turkey. The only thing I did different was grate some carrots into the recipe to cook with it. It gave it extra color. And I also topped it with shaved carrot as a topping.

Outstanding! I've made this twice now, omitting the brown sugar and mai fun to make the filling lighter. Everyone (including the kids) was surprised at how good it is, even those who don't like ground turkey. I am making it a third time as a hot appetizer for Easter dinner.

I added some red, orange and yellow pepper diced extremely fine to the ground turkey mixture a few minutes before it was finished cooking. We ate the first servings on lettuce, as in the recipe. Since there are only two of us, we had leftover meat and noodle which I mixed together and refrigerated. My husband decided to heat it up and snack on the leftovers with some whole wheat (100 calorie bread round) toast. It was spectacular. The flavors became better with time to blend. We especially loved the subtle orange zest flavor mixed with the savory onion and garlic and cilantro.s

I felt like I was eating at a great Thai restaurant! I had stellar results when following this recipe exactly as written. I'll probably cut the orange zest in half next time but that is just personal preference. All of these flavors are excellent together and it doesn't need changing. Easily feeds 4. Thank you blancdeblanc for a great recipe! Just a note though, when cooking the rice I believe the recipe is supposed to say 6oz of mai fun rice noodles per 2 cups of water, the cooking instructions for the mai fun rice noodles were otherwise correct. You could also easily substitute different mushrooms without hurting the end result. And a $$ saving hint, shop at your local asian market and you will find most of the ingredients for this recipe sometimes 1/2 the cost of supermarkets - especially dried mushrooms you just reconstitute and use.

I didn’t include the sugar and it was delicious! I doubled the recipe to have leftovers and it’s all gone! My kids hate mushrooms and didn’t say a word, I don’t think they even noticed they were too busy gobbling it down.

Very tasty. I messed with the seasonings a bit as I like my food to be on the spicier side. Extra ginger and I added about 2 tbs sambal (chili paste) to the meat and veggie mix while cooking. Also served it with a dipping sauce made from hoisin with a little sambal and rice vinegar. Will definitely use this again.
Yes they are a bit of work with all the chopping but well worth the time. I used regular mushrooms and used sesame oil instead of vegetable oil.
left out the noodles, orange zest and half of the ginger root - used baby bellas instead of shiitake, because that is what I had on hand. Delicious!

Delicious! I made 1/2 recipe according to directions- the only thing I didn’t have was bean sprouts. Mine were very messy - would need to put less filling in or have bigger leaves for company but for just the two of us - we didn’t care!
Loved it! Really good, healthy, filling.
Very tasty. I made without mushrooms, water chestnuts and noodles. Easy recipe and I will make again
Sooo Yummy!
The whole family loved this recipe. I didn't have orange zest but it was still delicious.
I left out the brown sugar and vinegar. Add a squeeze of lime instead of the orange. It was very good and very healthy. I'll make it again.

These were delicious. Made it exactly as the recipe called for, except left out peanuts (personal preference) and bean sprouts (didn't have any). Will make this again and again. Thank you for sharing, blancdeblanc!
Great recipe I used cremini mushrooms raw sugar and apple cider vinegar as substitutes as that is what I had.
Bria didn't like too much
